newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Spreads lack clear direction.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Spreads lack clear direction.

text.p: Australian semi-government bond yields generally mirrored the stable tone of the Australian Treasury market in the past week, although yield spreads between them were fairly mixed, traders said on Monday.
"Spreads have been fairly volatile in the past few months with no definite trend and seem to be more or less driven on the flows at the time," one trader added.

Australian debt markets could be in for a slow first half of the week with no major data due, although Thursday's Reserve Bank quarterly Bulletin will be heavily scanned for an indication on the central bank's policy thinking.
A 50 basis point cut in official interest rates has been priced in, but this move is not expected to come to fruitiion until after next week's quarterly inflation and wages data.
The RBA board meets on November 5.
Meanwhile, Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) said it will close its offer of switching into its new line of August 2008 bonds at 4.30 p.m (0630).
TCV issued the 2008 stock last week with a A$200 million debut tender but also allowed switching from other TCV issues to boost liquidity in the new line.
By 1.45 p.m. the stock stood at some A$563 million.
The new stock, which pays a 7.5 percent coupon, fetched an average yield of 7.86 percent and an 18.5 basis point margin over the government bond market.
"It went close enough to where people were expecting, but there hasn't been a lot of trade in the secondary market since," one trader said.
"The consolidation went fairly slowly on the day it was offered, but they (TCV) look to be fairly happy with the eventual result," he added.

Fresh supply into the Australian debt market is expected to be on hold for the time being after just over a A$1.0 billion of issuance last week with the Treasury tendering both fixed rate and indexed bonds, along with TCV's 2008 offering.

This could see Queensland Treasury Corporation's (QTC), which is getting close to its usual 4-6 week tender window, hold off until after next week's data, and possible after the RBA board meeting, traders added.
